title: DEM MPs Make First Post-Law İmralı Visit as PKK Disarmament Looms; Ankara Launches Nationwide LGBT Crackdown
subhead: A DEM Party delegation visited jailed PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan on İmralı on Sept. 13 — the first such meeting since parliament passed the PKK disarmament framework law in August — while Ankara simultaneously rolled out a sweeping operation against LGBT organizations and activists. Foreign Minister Fidan, meanwhile, used a Damascus trip to accuse Israel of destabilizing Syria.

sections.heading: Kurdish Peace Process: First İmralı Visit Since Disarmament Law
sections.body:
A DEM Party delegation led by lawmakers Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, accompanied by lawyer Faik Özgür Erol, traveled to the high-security prison island of İmralı on Sept. 13 to meet jailed PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan, according to Hürriyet Daily News. The meeting was the first since parliament approved, on Aug. 10, the 12-article framework law facilitating the PKK's disarmament and dissolution — legislation backed by 468 lawmakers, with all parties except the İYİ (Good) Party supporting it.

The law's measures take effect only after security agencies verify the PKK/KCK no longer maintains an operational presence and has surrendered all weapons, a finding that must be endorsed by the National Security Council and published in the Official Gazette. Last week, Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş said the PKK would begin disarming and handing over weapons to Iraq's central government in October. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zeidi separately said PKK-affiliated elements in the Sinjar region would begin handing over weapons, with Mount Sinjar returning to full federal control. The delegation's previous visit to Öcalan was on Aug. 2.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the first concrete post-law interaction between the DEM Party and Öcalan, signaling that the 'terror-free Türkiye' track is moving from legislation toward implementation — with October set as the disarmament deadline and Iraq's federal government drawn in as the receiving party for surrendered weapons.

sections.heading: Domestic Crackdown: 'My Family is Safe' LGBT Operation
sections.body:
Turkish authorities launched a sweeping operation on Sept. 13 targeting LGBT activists, organizations and venues, with proceedings initiated over allegations of obscenity, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek announced on X. Hürriyet Daily News reports that under the banner of the 'My Family is Safe' operations, legal proceedings were initiated against 162 suspects, nine organizations and 13 companies across 15 provinces, including Istanbul and Ankara.

Police raided entertainment venues in Istanbul, and access was blocked to the social media accounts of LGBT rights organizations, think tanks and university student clubs. Gürlek framed the move under the government's 'Year of the Family' campaign, citing protection of 'children, the institution of the family and social order.' He also said an investigation was opened into six LGBT organizations in Istanbul, with scrutiny of foreign funding: a MASAK (Financial Crimes Investigation Board) report flagged financial support from foreign individuals, foundations, embassies and public institutions.
sections.whyItMatters: The operation marks an escalation in the ruling camp's social-conservative agenda — combining legal proceedings, internet blocks and foreign-funding scrutiny of civil society — a move likely to draw sharp criticism from Western capitals and human rights groups at a moment when Ankara is courting Western goodwill on defense and the Kurdish process.

sections.heading: Foreign Policy: Fidan in Damascus Accuses Israel of Destabilizing Syria
sections.body:
Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, on a two-day official visit to Damascus beginning around Sept. 13, accused Israel of seeking to destabilize Syria through its attacks and of supporting 'terrorist organizations such as ISIL,' according to Hürriyet Daily News. 'Israel's policies are the biggest obstacle to the positive momentum in the fight against terrorism,' Fidan said at a joint press conference with Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani.

Fidan reiterated Ankara's support for the government in Damascus and said President Erdoğan was planning to visit Syria in the near future, without a specific date. On the integration of the SDF into the Syrian government, Fidan called the SDF's declaration on disbanding itself 'important and valuable,' adding that 'this step needs to be implemented without delay.' He is expected to meet President Ahmad al-Sharaa and Interior Minister Enes Hattab during the visit.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara is doubling down on its bet on Damascus — backing the Syrian government, pressing for swift SDF dissolution and positioning itself against Israel's Syria operations — while signaling an imminent Erdoğan visit that would cement Turkey's role as the new Syria's principal external patron.

sections.heading: Defense & US Ties: Congressman Floats S-400 Transfer to UAE for F-35 Return
sections.body:
US Congressman Darrel Issa, who visited Ankara in early September and was hosted by President Erdoğan and FM Fidan, suggested that transferring Turkey's Russian-made S-400 air defense systems to the United Arab Emirates could resolve the long-running rift with Washington and allow Ankara to reenter the F-35 program, Hürriyet Daily News reports from an interview published Sept. 10.

Issa cited prior Turkey-US-UAE talks on re-exporting the systems, saying 'this might be the best solution.' On sanctions, he echoed President Trump's July promise to lift CAATSA penalties once Turkey gives up the S-400s, insisting 'there are no sanctions against Türkiye.' He prioritized F-16 modernization over new F-35 sales, noting the huge order backlog. Turkey has agreed to buy 40 new F-16s, with negotiations ongoing over pricing, and has assigned TUSAŞ to upgrade its existing F-16 fleet.
sections.whyItMatters: A UAE re-export of the S-400s would be a face-saving off-ramp for all sides — clearing Turkey's path back into the F-35 ecosystem and removing the CAATSA cloud, while letting Ankara claim it did not scrap the systems outright. Issa's comments suggest the idea has congressional traction ahead of the F-16 pricing talks.

sections.heading: Foreign Relations: Ankara Denounces US Extension of Greek Cyprus Embargo Waiver
sections.body:
The Turkish Foreign Ministry denounced Washington's decision to extend the lifting of its arms embargo on the Greek Cypriot administration until Sept. 30, 2027, arguing the policy damages trust between the island's communities, Hürriyet Daily News reports. Ankara said it shared the views of the TRNC Foreign Ministry and stressed that steps eroding trust should be avoided while the Greek Cypriot side is 'increasing pressure in every field' on Turkish Cypriots, whom it called co-owners of the island.

The ministry said the Greek Cypriot side's intensified armament activities were harming regional stability, and reiterated that Turkey would defend Turkish Cypriots' rights and security 'under all circumstances.' Turkish Cyprus expressed 'deep regret' over the extension, urging consideration of the 'delicate balances' in the eastern Mediterranean amid ongoing Middle East conflicts.
sections.whyItMatters: The extended waiver, coming as Ankara pushes for a two-state settlement and upgraded Eastern Mediterranean posture, sharpens the US-Turkey friction point on Cyprus — though the rhetoric remained calibrated, stopping short of concrete retaliation.

sections.heading: Domestic Politics: Özel Leads New Party Rally After Üsküdar Loss to AKP
sections.body:
New Party leader Özgür Özel held a rally in Istanbul's Üsküdar district on Sept. 12, vowing to win back the municipality from the AKP at the ballot box, Hürriyet Daily News reports. The district's municipal council elected an AKP candidate as interim mayor on Sept. 8, after opposition Mayor Sinem Dedetaş was arrested on Aug. 31 over alleged corruption — handing the AKP control of a key Istanbul district.

Özel — who resigned as CHP chair on July 24 and broke away with 91 lawmakers to form the New Party — told supporters not to 'lose heart' and called for democratic unity, saying Türkiye had entered a new political era.
sections.whyItMatters: The Üsküdar flip, following arrests of opposition mayors and the earlier İmamoğlu conviction, shows the AKP consolidating municipal control amid the opposition's fragmentation — while Özel's vow to reclaim the district frames the New Party as the opposition's electoral vehicle.

bottomLine: On Sept. 14, Turkey moved forward on its most consequential political track even as it escalated a separate social crackdown. The DEM Party's first İmralı visit since the August disarmament law — with PKK weapon handovers to Iraq's central government slated for October — suggests the 'terror-free Türkiye' process is shifting from legislation to implementation. In a parallel move, Ankara launched a nationwide 'My Family is Safe' operation against LGBT organizations, venues and 162 suspects, with foreign-funding scrutiny that is set to test Western tolerance. Fidan's Damascus trip, accusing Israel of destabilizing Syria while pressing for swift SDF dissolution, points to an imminent Erdoğan visit cementing Turkey as the new Syria's chief patron. Meanwhile, a US congressman's push for a UAE S-400 transfer could offer the clearest path yet back into the F-35 program.
sources: Hürriyet Daily News, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency
